title: Personal Project Ideas Maths Students Can Build
summary: Personal Project ideas maths: explore nine practical options, set learning and product goals, then turn one interest into a focused MYP project plan today.
body_markdown:
A strong maths MYP Personal Project connects something you want to understand with something you can create and test. These **Personal Project ideas maths** students can develop range from fair board games to budgeting tools, mathematical art and sports analysis.


Perhaps a game feels unfair, or you wonder whether football statistics predict performance. That curiosity becomes useful when you separate two goals: what you want to learn and what you intend to produce. RevisionDojo’s guide to[setting a strong MYP Personal Project goal](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/strong-myp-personal-project-goal) explains how to connect them.


### A quick project selection checklist


Before committing, ask:


- Does this connect maths to a personal interest?
- What mathematical knowledge will I develop?
- Can I create a specific product or outcome?
- Is it feasible with my time, materials and skills?
- Can I define testable success criteria?
- Will research, testing and revision generate useful evidence?


A focused investigation gives you more room to explain decisions than an enormous topic you cannot test.


### Nine Personal Project ideas for maths students


Adapt these starting points to your interests, audience and available resources.


Project idea Learning goal Product goal


Design a fair board game Explore probability, expected value and game balance. Create a playable game, rulebook and testing record.


Model architectural geometry Investigate proportion, symmetry, scale and design constraints. Build a scale model or digital design with annotated calculations.


Build a budgeting tool Understand percentages, compound growth and spending assumptions. Create a spreadsheet for a defined audience’s monthly budget.


Investigate sports performance Examine averages, distributions, correlation and data limitations.
